audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..3].side read 'Skill' while content win[0..3] read 'Xerath' — the page rendered two different answers for the first four rows.
audit.why: The packet levelChart is Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Skill/Skill/Skill, the content layer already matches it, and the phase whys for those rows describe Xerath winning. Xerath's charged Q reaches past Lux's 1175 Light Binding, so the early range lead is real; from 6 both ults land and it flattens.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side moved to Xerath with ratings raised to 7/10; rows 4-6 left at Skill, where both layers already agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike did not say what actually decides it: Final Spark punishing the Rite of the Arcane channel.
audit.why: Xerath's R is a channel that immobilises him and any CC cancels it, so a landed Light Binding at the wrong moment ends the ult outright. Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 and 40s at rank 3.
audit.corrected: breakdown.mid and breakdown.cooldowns now key the R commit to Light Binding being down.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were missing entirely: Prismatic Barrier absorbing the burst window, and Illumination's auto-attack reset being the real tell for her combo.
audit.why: Prismatic Barrier is 12s at rank 1 and shields on both the outbound and return pass, so burst spent before it is out is burst wasted. Illumination charges on any damaging spell and detonates on her next attack, so the auto wind-up — not the spell cast — is the cue to step back.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d now says to force the shield first; dontsFull[0].d now names Illumination as the tell.

audit.why: Light Binding is a flat 10 seconds at every rank, which is the single number this whole matchup is played around, and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: Light Binding 10s, Shocking Orb 13s, Final Spark 60s->40s.

notes: Chart repaired: full phases[0..3].side said 'Skill' while content win[0..3] said 'Xerath'. Ratings on those rows raised 5/10 to 7/10 to match the new side. Rows 4-6 are 'Skill' in both layers and were left alone.
